nushell_command_list.use: names of commands/docs/*.md; a Nu-side head counts as a builtin only if it is in this list

method: Rows of the 'Command Equivalents' table in coming_from_bash.md and of nushell_map.md (Bash column). Bash side: leading utility of each backticked snippet (placeholders like 'command' skipped). Nu side: head of each pipeline stage of each backticked snippet that names a Nushell builtin (longest match against the command list). When a cell lists the same number of alternatives on both sides they are paired in order; otherwise every Bash alternative gets every Nu command of the row. Rows with an empty Bash cell continue the row above.

alias.row: | `alias s="git status -sb"`           | `alias s = git status -sb`                                    | Define an alias temporarily                                       |

bash.row: | `bash <script file>`                 | `nu <script file>`                                            | Run a script file                                                 |

cargo.row: | `cargo b --jobs=$(nproc)`            | `cargo b $"--jobs=(sys cpu \| length)"`                       | Use command output in an option                                   |

cat.row: | `cat <path>`                         | `open --raw <path>`                                           | Display the contents of the given file                            |
|                                      | `open <path>`                                                 | Read a file as structured data                                    |
| `cat <(<command1>) <(<command2>)`    | `[(command1), (command2)] \| str join`                        | Concatenate the outputs of command1 and command2                  |
| `cat <path> <(<command>)`            | `[(open --raw <path>), (command)] \| str join`                | Concatenate the contents of the given file and output of command  |

compgen.row: | `compgen -c`                         | `which`                                                       | List every Nushell command and every executable in PATH           |

cp.row: | `cp -r <source> <dest>`              | `cp -r <source> <dest>`                                       | Copy directory to a new location, recursively                     |

date.row: | `date -d "tomorrow"`                 | `"tomorrow" \| date from-human`                               | Parse a human-readable date                                       |
|                                      | `date from-human --list`                                      | Show example phrases that `date from-human` understands           |

echo.row: | `echo /tmp/$RANDOM`                  | `$"/tmp/(random int)"`                                        | Use command output in a string                                    |
| `echo $?`                            | `$env.LAST_EXIT_CODE`                                         | See the exit status of the last executed command                  |
| `echo ${FOO:-fallback}`              | `$env.FOO? \| default "ABC"`                                  | Use a fallback in place of an unset variable                      |
| `pwd` or `echo $PWD`                 | `pwd` or `$env.PWD`                                           | Display the current directory (`pwd` returns `$env.PWD`)          |

export.row: | `export FOO=BAR`                     | `$env.FOO = "BAR"`                                            | Set environment variable for current session                      |

find.row: | `find . -name *.rs`                  | `ls **/*.rs`                                                  | Find recursively all files that match a given pattern             |
| `find . -name Makefile \| xargs vim` | `ls **/Makefile \| get name \| vim ...$in`                    | Pass values as command parameters                                 |

for.row: | `for f in *.md; do echo $f; done`    | `ls *.md \| each { $in.name }`                                | Iterate over a list and return results                            |
for.bash: for f in *.md; do echo $f; done

for.row: | `for i in $(seq 1 10); do echo $i; done` | `for i in 1..10 { print $i }`                             | Iterate over a list and run a command on results                  |
for.bash: for i in $(seq 1 10); do echo $i; done

grep.row: | `grep <pattern>`                     | `where $it =~ <substring>` or `find <substring>`              | Filter strings that contain the substring                         |
| `grep <pattern>`                     | `where $it =~ <substring>` or `find <substring>`              | Filter strings that contain the substring                         |
| `grep -i <pattern>`                  | `find -i <substring>`                                         | Filter strings that contain the substring, ignoring case          |
| `grep -o <regex>`                    | `find -o -r <regex>`                                          | Output only the matched text, one value per match                 |
| `grep -v <pattern>`                  | `find -v <substring>`                                         | Filter strings that don't contain the substring                   |

head.row: | `command \| head -5`                 | `command \| first 5`                                          | Limit the output to the first 5 rows of an internal command (see also `last` and `skip`) |

less.row: | `command 2>&1 \| less`               | `command out+err>\| less` or `command o+e>\| less`            | Pipe stdout and stderr of an external command into less (NOTE: use [explore](explore.html) for paging output of internal commands) |

| `ls -la`                             | `ls --long --all` or `ls -la`                                 | List files with all available information, including hidden files |

mkdir.row: | `mkdir -p <path>`                    | `mkdir <path>`                                                | Creates the given path, creating parents as necessary             |

pwd.row: | `pwd` or `echo $PWD`                 | `pwd` or `$env.PWD`                                           | Display the current directory (`pwd` returns `$env.PWD`)          |
| `pwd -P`                             | `pwd -P` or `pwd --physical`                                  | Display the current directory with symbolic links resolved        |
| `pwd -P`                             | `pwd -P` or `pwd --physical`                                  | Display the current directory with symbolic links resolved        |

read.row: | `read var`                           | `let var = input`                                             | Get input from the user                                           |
| `read -s secret`                     | `let secret = input -s`                                       | Get a secret value from the user without printing keystrokes      |

rm.row: |                                      | `rm -t <path>`                                                | Move the given file to the system trash                           |

sed.row: | `sed`                                | `str replace`                                                 | Find and replace a pattern in a string                            |

tee.row: | `cmd1 \| tee log.txt \| cmd2`        | `cmd1 \| tee { save log.txt } \| cmd2`                        | Tee command output to a log file                                  |

type.row: | `type FOO`                           | `which FOO`                                                   | Display information about a command (builtin, alias, or executable) |
| `type -a FOO`                        | `which -a FOO`                                                | List the Nushell command and each executable in PATH with that name |
| `type -P FOO`                        | `which ^FOO`                                                  | Look up only the external program, skipping Nushell commands      |

unset.row: | `unset FOO`                          | `hide-env FOO`                                                | Unset environment variable for current session                    |
